newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TRANZ RAIL SHARES LEAP ON AN SPECULATION.
newsitem.headline: TRANZ RAIL SHARES LEAP ON AN SPECULATION.

text.p: Shares in New Zealand railway operator Tranz Rail leapt 30 cents to NZ$8.60 at the local open on Thursday after their ADRs surged on Wall Street overnight.
Analysts said speculation that Tranz Rail may be close to sealing an acquisition within the privatisation of Australian National Railways (AN) was behind the share price movement.

"Basically some brokers in the States were talking around clients about it and were basically saying they thought it would be a positive move for the company," said John Cobb, analyst at JB Were and Son.

"They know that the company is interested in doing it, the company has made noises in the past that certainly the Australian Railways would be of interest to them, but there's been nothing more specific than that."
About 50 groups, including Tranz Rail, have lodged interest in the sale of all or parts of AN, the loss making rail operation which the Australian government is privatising.
A Tranz Rail spokesperson confirmed that the company had been shortlisted by the federal government and had conducted due diligence, but declined to comment further.
AN is the remainder of the federal government's rail operations left after profitable elements were merged with some state services to form the National Rail Corporation in 1993.

Track ownership has also been separated from AN and what is left is a collection of freight and passenger services burdened with more than A$1 (NZ$1.16) billion in debt. It is expected to lose A$250 million in the fiscal year to June 30.
The Australian government invited bids earlier this year and said it would inject A$2 billion into AN to free it from debt.
Tranz Rail has said it is keen to buy AN's assets, possibly in conjunction with its U.S. shareholder Wisconsin Central Transportation .
Cobb said Wisconsin's involvement with Tranz Rail, in which it has a 22.6 percent holding, made the stock more attractive to U.S investors.

"U.S. investors seem to have a very strong attraction to the stock, particularly with Wisconsin being in there as a major shareholder...they have been very successful in the States with the companies they've been involved with there," he said.

"I think U.S. investors believe that with Wisconsin involved with Tranz Rail they'll be just another success story. That's really where it's at and I guess the locals are really just jumping on that bandwagon."
Tranz Rail opened at NZ$8.60 but fell five cents in early trade to $8.55, up 25 cents on volume of 285,890 shares.
